topSignals.title: FERC Generation Adequacy Reports due today (July 20) — first public quantification of firm-power gap by region
topSignals.text: — All six RTOs/ISOs (PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, NYISO, ISO-NE) must file informational reports by today detailing how adequate generation will serve new large loads (≥50 MW), with stakeholder proposals, milestone schedules, and ongoing proceedings. These filings — the direct product of the June 18 Section 206 show cause orders — represent the first regulator-mandated public estimate of the generation shortfall in each US grid region. Any region projecting a >5-year queue backlog with no credible near-term supply addition is, in effect, a validated and quantified SOFC addressable market. Actual filing content will become accessible in FERC eLibrary (docket RM26-4) once submitted; extract the confirmed large-load MW seeking grid connection per region as the first objective measure of the SOFC grid-bypass TAM. FERC RM26-4 docket | McGuireWoods briefing | Troutman analysis

topSignals.title: Siemens + FuelCell Energy EBOP MOU: first full coverage (announced July 9)
topSignals.text: — Mentioned briefly in the July 19 digest; first substantive coverage today. Siemens signed a non-binding MOU with FuelCell Energy on July 9, 2026 to design and supply electrical balance-of-plant (EBOP) systems for FCEL fuel cell installations targeting 100+ MW commercial projects for data centers. Siemens contributes: switchgear, transformers, protection systems, grid interconnection equipment, battery energy storage, and microgrid controls. FCEL provides the 12.5 MW MCFC Energy Block generation assets. No financial terms disclosed. Strategic significance: Siemens's EBOP standardization reduces per-project site electrical engineering effort — a meaningful cost and timeline advantage for multi-hundred-MW deployments. Competitor context: Bloom Energy handles EBOP integration internally; the Siemens partnership attempts to give FCEL a comparable systems-integration capability. GlobeNewswire | Siemens PR | DCD

topSignals.title: Aalo Atomics: Microsoft-backed 4th microreactor reaches criticality July 4 — 10 MWe full-scale core targeting 50 MWe AI data center "Pods"
topSignals.text: — Aalo Atomics' Critical Test Reactor achieved initial criticality at Idaho National Laboratory on July 4, 2026 at 12:20 a.m. MT, becoming the fourth advanced reactor to meet EO 14301's deadline — and the most commercially relevant for AI data centers. Unlike the first three zero-power demonstrators (Antares Mark-0, Valar Ward 250, Deployable Energy Unity), Aalo's CTR includes a full-scale nuclear core for a 10 MWe commercial unit, which will be aggregated into 50 MWe "Aalo Pods" targeting co-location with AI data centers near the Idaho National Laboratory and beyond. Microsoft is an investor. Announced July 6, 2026. The 10 MWe per-unit scale and data-center-specific co-location design make Aalo the first microreactor with an explicit architecture for AI workloads — and the most direct nuclear competitor to SOFC in the <100 MW modular on-site segment, albeit with a ~2028-2031 commercial delivery horizon. BusinessWire | DCD | World Nuclear News | Interesting Engineering

items.text: SolydEra EFCF 2026 paper: DynElectro 23,000-hour stack result and PMX 10 kW generator (first full coverage) — The EFCF 2026 proceedings include a SolydEra/DynElectro paper (available on efcf.com) documenting 23,000 hours of stable SOFC stack operation by Danish partner DynElectro using a SolydEra G8X 4.5 kW stack in steam electrolysis mode; operation ceased July 2025 due to a system-related failure (not stack failure). Separately, SolydEra has scaled the G8X stack platform to 10 kW (30 kW in SOEC mode) and developed the PMX modular 10 kW generator: a compact containerized unit using SolydEra stacks and a proprietary 10 kW hot balance-of-plant. A H2-capable PMX variant was developed under the Italian GreenH2Building project and is scheduled for field installation by end-June 2026 at a partner site in southern Italy — first real-world deployment of the PMX. Power density: 7 kW/m² (rising to 10.5 kW/m² in the planned 60 kW successor). Tested electrical efficiency: 60%; total efficiency with heat recovery: 84%. SolydEra EFCF 2026 paper | NAUTILUS project

Elcogen E3000 G2 cycling durability: 23,000 rapid current cycles with performance improvement — Post-EFCF company data confirms that the E3000 G2 was subjected to 23,000 rapid current-cycling events in electrolysis mode during testing; the stack showed performance improvement (not degradation) throughout. Additionally, no degradation was observed in thermal cycling tests. This cycling durability is directly relevant for data center applications requiring load-following. Stated specs remain: 75% electrical / 90% CHP efficiency at 650°C; 119-cell stack; fuel-flexible (NG, biogas, H2); SOEC 33 kWh/kg H2 mode. Commercial-condition stack efficiency benchmarks from the EFCF are still not publicly available. Elcogen product page | ResearchGate abstract

EFCF embargo: day 17 — No commercial-scale efficiency or degradation benchmarks from Elcogen, Ceres licensees (Doosan), or Convion have been published online. Watch elcogen.com, ceres.tech, and convion.fi.

FERC RM26-4 generation adequacy filings: today is the deadline — See Top Signal #1. Six RTOs/ISOs must file today in FERC eLibrary; content will be the first official regional sizing of the large-load firm-power gap. ISO-NE filed a 90-day abeyance request; if granted, its filing moves to ~August 3 with full tariff reform due August 17. Filings from PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, and NYISO are expected today. Any RTO that establishes a self-supply exemption analogous to ERCOT's Batch Zero pathway will codify a $5-20/MWh avoided-transmission-charge benefit for SOFC grid-bypass projects in that region. FERC RM26-4 | Day Pitney

New York legislature formally passes moratorium — The New York State Legislature passed the first-in-the-nation data center moratorium into statute (Harris Beach Murtha, July 2026). EO No. 62 (signed July 14) is now codified: one-year pause on DEC discretionary permits for new hyperscale data centers ≥50 MW; Energize NY DPS proceeding to define self-supply requirements. Full background in July 19 digest. Harris Beach Murtha

Background: Germany EnEfG PUE ≤ 1.2 active from July 1; EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed into Q3; Section 179D sunset confirmed; ITC 48E 30% credit active; ERCOT Batch Zero self-supply pathway active.

Aalo Atomics (Microsoft-backed): 10 MWe modules, 50 MWe Pods for AI data centers — See Top Signal #3. Aalo is the first advanced nuclear company to design a modular unit explicitly sized for AI data center co-location. The 10 MWe per-core / 50 MWe per-Pod architecture is closer in scale to SOFC modular arrays than the 390 MW IMSR (Terrestrial Energy) or 1.1 GW AP1000. Competitive assessment: Aalo still operates a zero-power CTR (no commercial electricity dispatch). Commercial Pod deployment is targeted for "the AI data center era" but no confirmed timeline or PPA has been announced. Competitive risk for SOFC: moderate at the <100 MW modular segment, emerging ~2028-2031. BusinessWire | Interesting Engineering

Background: Microsoft Project Kilby 2.67 GW CCGT (Texas, first power 2028), DOE $17.5B AP1000 nuclear loan programme (10 units, 2030+ construction start), Google Meitner Energy Center (renewables + gas firming, TX Panhandle), Terrestrial Energy/Riot Platforms 4 GW IMSR (early 2030s) — all covered in prior digests.

Bloom Energy (BE) — Last confirmed close: ~$206.73-216 range (Friday July 18/Monday July 19 data points); GurFocus article noted a +4.2% session gain (likely July 18 recovery). As of today's session (July 20), BE is 8 days from Q2 earnings (July 28, AH); consensus: ~$804M revenue / $0.36 EPS / ~34% gross margin. Stock testing the $200-220 range as the market waits for the July 28 print to reset the execution-risk narrative. GurFocus session note | StockInvest

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) — Approximately $17, -19% from the $21 July 9 offering price. Siemens EBOP MOU (see Top Signal #2) is the most recent positive catalyst. Torrington expansion ($225M raised via July 9 offering, 350-500 MW/year by H2 2027) funded. Analyst range: B. Riley Buy $32 | Jefferies Buy $24 | UBS Neutral $22. Data center proposals: >80% of 1.5 GW active pipeline. Q3 FY2026 earnings ~September 2026.

SolydEra EFCF 2026 paper: PMX modular generator system architecture — See Stack & Cell Technology above. Compact PMX unit design (10 kW hotbop + 10 kW G8X stack) is the most detailed public disclosure of SolydEra's product architecture to date. The 84% total efficiency (electrical + heat) at 60% electrical in the NAUTILUS Finland 40 kW prototype (tested December 2023) is the closest real-world benchmark. EFCF SolydEra paper

Elcogen E3000 G2 cycling resilience — 23,000 rapid current cycles in electrolysis mode with performance improvement is the key durability data point now in the public domain from EFCF 2026. Reinforces the load-following suitability argument for reversible SOFC deployments at AI data centers with variable renewable co-generation. Elcogen
EFCF embargo continues on full commercial-conditions efficiency data from Elcogen, Ceres licensees, SolydEra, and Convion. Day 17 post-conference.

lcoe.text: FERC filing content (extract today): once the RM26-4 generation adequacy reports are accessible in FERC eLibrary, extract: (a) total confirmed large-load MW in queue per RTO that cannot be served within 5 years, and (b) any explicit reference to self-supply exemption mechanisms. The per-RTO shortfall is the first regulatory-grade quantification of the US SOFC grid-bypass TAM.

Siemens EBOP bundling: potential $200-500/kW site-engineering cost reduction — Standardized EBOP supply (switchgear, transformers, microgrid controls) from a single Tier-1 OEM reduces per-project site electrical engineering costs and compression timelines. For SOFC-vs-MCFC LCOE comparisons, if FCEL/Siemens can match Bloom's integrated delivery model, the deployment cost premium for MCFC narrows. No specific cost-per-kW savings disclosed yet; watch for FCEL Q3 FY2026 (September) for any project-level economics.

SolydEra PMX: 84% total efficiency benchmark at 60% electrical — The NAUTILUS-tested figure is the most current real-world European SOFC system efficiency data point. At 60% electrical and 84% total: CHP heat-monetization credit in the LCOE model is ~0.24 kWh thermal per kWh electrical produced, at district heat or process-steam value of €30-60/MWh thermal. For German DC projects subject to EnEfG ERF ≥ 10% (now active), this 24% thermal capture exceeds the 10% ERF threshold well into the ≥20% (2028) target — confirming SOFC CHP compliance value.

Aalo Atomics: 50 MWe Pod unit cost TBD — At commercial scale, 10 MWe units aggregated to 50 MWe Pods will have different capex characteristics than AP1000 nuclear (>$6,000/kW) or IMSR (TBD). No published capex estimate; maintain SOFC as the default on-site power assumption for <100 MW AI data center projects through at least 2030.

BE earnings July 28 — 8 days: the sole near-term fundamental reset. Key model inputs to extract: (a) manufacturing cost per kW at 2 GW Fremont run rate, (b) product gross margin vs. ~34% guidance, (c) EaaS $/MWh pricing from Nebius/Brookfield deployments, (d) Project Jupiter delivery milestone commentary, (e) any FY2026 guidance revision.
